definition_zh: 以实验方式；实验性地；在实验中；通过实验证明地
definition_en: by means of an experiment, or in a tentative way that is still being tested
core_image: 一只手在记录本上写下“第 3 次试验”，旁边是刚刚调好的仪器刻度。
scene: 论文的方法部分说明这个效应不是靠推算。 The methods section says the effect was measured experimentally rather than inferred.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 experimentally 是「通过实验方式测定」（第 1、8 个义项）；句意：方法部分写明，这个效应是通过实验测得的，而不是靠推算。

pos.zh: 以实验方式；实验性地；通过实验地

senses.title: By experimental means
senses.titleCN: 以实验方式：靠动手试验而非推理
senses.definition: by carrying out an experiment rather than by reasoning alone
senses.definitionCN: 通过进行实验而非仅靠推理地
senses.example: The hypothesis was tested experimentally, not argued from first principles.
senses.exampleCN: 该假设是通过实验检验的，而不是从基本原理推出来的。
senses.why: The adverb answers the question How was this found out? The answer is a procedure: someone built a test and ran it.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词回答‘这是怎么知道的？’答案是程序：有人搭了测试并运行它。

senses.title: In the course of an experiment
senses.titleCN: 在实验中：作为实验过程的一部分
senses.definition: in the course of an experiment, as part of its procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在实验过程中，作为其程序的一部分
senses.example: The samples were handled experimentally under sterile conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这些样本在无菌条件下按实验规程处理。
senses.why: Here the adverb places an action inside the experiment: the action is not merely tested, it belongs to the test's internal sequence.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词把动作放进实验内部：该动作不只是被检验，它属于实验内部的步骤序列。

senses.title: Confirmed by experiment
senses.titleCN: 经实验证明地：结果站住了
senses.definition: in a way that has been confirmed by experimental results
senses.definitionCN: 已被实验结果确认地
senses.example: The prediction was confirmed experimentally in two independent labs.
senses.exampleCN: 该预测在两个独立实验室中经实验得到确认。
senses.why: The adverb can mark epistemic status: the claim is not just tested but has passed the test, at least so far.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以标记认识论地位：该主张不只是被测试，而是通过了测试，至少截至目前。

senses.title: Tentatively, as a trial
senses.titleCN: 试验性地：先试一段时间再定
senses.definition: in a tentative way, as a trial rather than a final arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 以试探方式，作为试验而非最终安排地
senses.example: The team experimentally moved the meeting to Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 团队试验性地把会议改到了周五。
senses.why: Here the word has escaped the laboratory: any provisional action can be done experimentally, with the option of reversing it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词已经离开实验室：任何暂定行动都可以 experimental 地做，并保留撤回的选项。

senses.title: Methodologically
senses.titleCN: 在方法上：用实验法而非观察法
senses.definition: with respect to experimental method, as opposed to observation or theory
senses.definitionCN: 就实验方法而言，相对于观察或理论地
senses.example: The two groups were compared experimentally and statistically.
senses.exampleCN: 两组分别从实验和统计上作了比较。
senses.why: The adverb can distinguish a methodology from its neighbours: field observation records what happens, experimental work makes something happen.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以把一种方法论与邻居区分开：野外观察记录发生什么，实验工作则让某事发生。

senses.title: In a clinical trial
senses.titleCN: 在临床试验中：作为受试方案
senses.definition: as part of a clinical trial or an investigational treatment
senses.definitionCN: 作为临床试验或研究性治疗的一部分地
senses.example: The patient was treated experimentally under a strict protocol.
senses.exampleCN: 病人在严格方案下接受了试验性治疗。
senses.why: Medicine uses the adverb for care delivered inside a trial, where the protocol defines what may and may not be done.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个副词指在试验内部提供的照护；方案定义了可以做什么、不可以做什么。

senses.title: In an experimental art practice
senses.titleCN: 在实验艺术中：以作品作为试验
senses.definition: in an avant-garde or trial-based artistic practice
senses.definitionCN: 以前卫或试验为基础的艺术实践中
senses.example: The composer worked experimentally with recorded noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作曲家以实验方式处理录制噪声。
senses.why: The adverb transfers the lab attitude to art: the work is made to see what happens, and failure is allowed to remain visible.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把实验室态度转到艺术上：作品被做出来是为了看会发生什么，失败被允许留在明处。

senses.title: Measured by experiment
senses.titleCN: 以实验测定地：数值来自装置
senses.definition: by a measurement obtained through experimental apparatus
senses.definitionCN: 通过实验装置获得的测量地
senses.example: The constant was determined experimentally to four decimal places.
senses.exampleCN: 该常数由实验测定到四位小数。
senses.why: Here the focus is the number's origin: it came from an instrument and a procedure, not from a table or a calculation.
senses.whyCN: 这里聚焦数值的来源：它来自仪器与程序，而不是表格或计算。

intro.en: Experimentally is experimental plus -ly. The adjective comes from experiment, from Latin experimentum, a trial. The suffix -ly descends from Old English -lice.
intro.cn: experimentally 是 experimental 加 -ly。形容词来自 experiment，源头是拉丁 experimentum‘试验’。后缀 -ly 源自古典英语 -lice。

items.en: To try or test. Its past participle expertus also gives English expert: an expert is literally someone who has tried things.
items.cn: 尝试、检验。其过去分词 expertus 也给出英语 expert：专家字面上就是‘试过事情的人’。

items.en: A trial, test, or proof. The noun names both the procedure and the evidence it produces.
items.cn: 试验、检验、证明。该名词既命名程序，也命名程序产生的证据。

items.en: Borrowed in the 14c. Its meaning narrowed as the controlled method developed: a trial that deliberately changes one variable.
items.cn: 14 世纪借入。随着受控方法发展，词义收窄为‘有意改变一个变量的试验’。

items.en: The adjective appears in the 17c with the rise of demonstrative science. It marks both the method and the provisional status of the result.
items.cn: 形容词随 17 世纪演示科学兴起而出现。它同时标记方法与结果的暂定地位。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly comes from Old English -lice, originally a distinct word meaning ‘body’ or ‘form’. It became the regular way to turn adjectives into manner adverbs.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 来自古典英语 -lice，原是一个意为‘身体、形态’的独立词，后来成为把形容词变方式副词的常规手段。

items.en: The adverb spread from scientific writing into medicine, management, and art, wherever an action is described as a trial rather than a settled practice.
items.cn: 这个副词从科学写作扩展到医学、管理与艺术：凡是把行动描述为试验而非既定做法的地方都能用。

note.en: The first group is the experiment family; the second compares adverbs for how a claim is established or how cautiously an action is taken.
note.cn: 第一组是 experiment 词族；第二组比较表示‘如何确立主张’或‘行动有多谨慎’的副词。

entries.definition: relating to or based on an experiment. The adverb applies that property to the manner of an action.
entries.definitionCN: 与实验有关或基于实验的；副词把这一属性加到动作方式上。

entries.definition: a test, or to carry out a test. The adverb says the action was done through such a test.
entries.definitionCN: 试验，或进行试验；副词说明动作是通过这种试验完成的。

entries.definition: the practice of experimenting. It is the activity; experimentally is the manner.
entries.definitionCN: 进行实验的实践；是活动，experimentally 是方式。

entries.definition: the person who runs the test. It names the agent behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 运行测试的人；命名副词背后的施动者。

entries.definition: by observation or experience rather than theory. It is broader than experimentally and includes field evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 通过观察或经验而非理论；比 experimentally 更宽，包含野外证据。

entries.definition: in a cautious, provisional way. It stresses hesitation rather than procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 以谨慎、暂定的方式；强调犹豫，而非程序。

entries.definition: in actual practice rather than in theory. It contrasts with theory, not with observation.
entries.definitionCN: 在实际做法中而非理论上；与理论相对，而非与观察相对。

entries.definition: by breaking a problem into parts. It is a desk method, often the opposite of hands-on testing.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题拆成部分来处理；是书桌方法，常与动手测试相对。

entries.definition: according to theory, or in principle. It marks the opposite source of knowledge to experimentally.
entries.definitionCN: 根据理论，或原则上；标记与 experimentally 相对的知识来源。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: experimental plus -ly. The adverb says the action was done through a trial, or as a trial.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：experimental 加 -ly。这个副词说明动作是通过试验完成的，或本身就作为试验。

normal.en: Experimental plus -ly: in the manner of a test.
normal.cn: experimental 加 -ly：以测试的方式。

normal.en: Measured experimentally: the number came out of a machine, not a table.
normal.cn: measured experimentally：数字来自机器，不是表格。

normal.en: Confirmed experimentally: the claim survived contact with apparatus.
normal.cn: confirmed experimentally：主张经受住了与仪器的接触。

normal.en: Treated experimentally: the protocol, not the clinic routine, decides.
normal.cn: treated experimentally：由方案决定，而不是门诊常规。

normal.en: Moved experimentally: try Friday, and be ready to move it back.
normal.cn: moved experimentally：先试周五，并准备好改回来。

abstract.en: Experimentally is a confession about the source of a claim: hands made it, not arguments.
abstract.cn: experimentally 是对主张来源的坦白：是手做出来的，不是论证出来的。

abstract.en: The adverb quietly ranks knowledge: what is experimentally shown can still be overturned by a better experiment.
abstract.cn: 这个副词在悄悄给知识排序：实验证明的东西，仍可能被更好的实验推翻。

abstract.en: A society that values experimentally also has to tolerate failure, because trial and failure are one word.
abstract.cn: 重视 experimentally 的社会也必须容忍失败，因为试验与失败是同一个词的两面。

examples.en: The viscosity was determined experimentally at three temperatures.
examples.cn: 黏度在三个温度下通过实验测定。

examples.en: They experimentally introduced a four-day week and measured the effect on output.
examples.cn: 他们试验性地引入四天工作制，并测量对产出的影响。

examples.en: The drug was used experimentally long before it was approved.
examples.cn: 这种药在获批之前很久就被试验性使用了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗死，配一闷头，里”——实验里一组死、一组闷头记录，里里外外都试过：experimentally 以实验方式。

root: 由 experimental 加 -ly 构成；experimental 源自拉丁 experimentum（试验），源头 experiri（尝试）。核心是“以试验的方式”或“作为试验地”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of experimentally, one answer to How: through a test, inside a test, confirmed by a test, as a test, by test method, in a trial, in experimental art, or by instrument. The manner changes; the trial remains.
sensesIntro.cn: experimentally 的八个义项都在回答‘如何’：通过试验、在试验内、经试验确认、作为试验、用实验法、在临床试验中、在实验艺术中、用仪器测定。方式在变，试验不变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand writing run number three beside a freshly set instrument.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在刚调好的仪器旁写下‘第三次试验’。

chain: THE ACTION IS DONE THROUGH TESTING

branches.en: THE METHOD: the claim is produced by procedure rather than by argument.
branches.cn: 方法：主张由程序产生，而非由论证产生。

branches.en: INSIDE THE TRIAL: actions belong to the protocol rather than to ordinary life.
branches.cn: 试验进程内：动作属于既定方案，而不属于日常生活。

branches.en: THE VERIFIED NUMBER: confirmation and measurement both trace back to apparatus.
branches.cn: 被验证的数值：确认与测量都追溯回仪器。

branches.en: THE PROVISIONAL ACT: a Friday meeting and a noise composition are both trials with reversible outcomes.
branches.cn: 暂定行动：周五会议与噪声作曲都是结果可撤回的试验。

branches.en: THE CONSENT FRAME: medicine uses the adverb to mark care delivered under study conditions.
branches.cn: 知情同意框架：医学用这个副词标记在研究条件下提供的照护。

intro.en: Experimentally is experimental plus -ly. The family runs from experiment and experimentation to experimentalist and experimenter.
intro.cn: experimentally 是 experimental 加 -ly。词族从 experiment、experimentation 延伸到 experimentalist 与 experimenter。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are experiri and experimentum, with the participle expertus behind English expert. The deeper per- connection is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 experiri 与 experimentum，分词 expertus 是英语 expert 的来源。更深的 per- 联系属重构。

items.example: They ran the experiment twice.

items.meaning: based on or belonging to a test
items.example: The design is still experimental.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计仍是试验性的。

items.example: The value was obtained experimentally.
items.exampleCN: 该数值是通过实验得到的。

items.example: Experimentation preceded the final design.
items.exampleCN: 在最终设计之前先进行了实验。

items.example: The experimenter changed the order of trials.
items.exampleCN: 实验者改变了试验顺序。

items.example: The composer is an experimentalist by habit.
items.exampleCN: 这位作曲家习惯上是实验派。

items.meaningCN: 专家；有经过检验的知识的人
items.example: An expert reviewed the apparatus.

items.meaningCN: 经验；从实践得来的知识
items.example: Experience is a long series of trials.
The sea ice was a known peril.
The descent was perilous in the dark.

definition_zh: 环礁；珊瑚环礁（由珊瑚礁围成环形、中间包着潟湖的海岛）
definition_en: a ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a shallow lagoon, often with low islets on the rim
core_image: 海面上一圈细细的白浪围住一片浅蓝，圈外是深蓝，圈内是平静的浅水
scene: 飞机下降时，海面浮出一圈白色浪线，中间围着一片浅蓝水面。 Below them an atoll ringed a shallow lagoon.
sceneCN: 这里 atoll 指「环形珊瑚礁及其围合的整体」（第 1 个义项：作为完整地貌单位的环礁）；句意为他们下方的一座环礁围着一片浅潟湖。

pos.zh: 环礁；珊瑚环礁（可数，复数 atolls）

derivatives.zh: atoll（环礁）+ lagoon（潟湖，意大利 laguna ← 拉丁 lacuna「水池」）→ 环礁潟湖：环礁围出的浅水区
atoll + reef（礁，古诺斯语 rif「脊」）→ 环礁礁体：构成环形的珊瑚礁带
cay（小沙岛，源自西班牙语 cayo，可能上溯加勒比语）→ 环礁礁缘上的低矮沙洲
atoll + -like（类似……的）→ 环礁状的：形状像环礁的

senses.title: A ring-shaped reef
senses.titleCN: 环形礁体：围合的整体地貌
senses.definition: a coral reef forming a closed or nearly closed ring
senses.definitionCN: 形成闭合或近于闭合环形的珊瑚礁
senses.example: Below them an atoll ringed a shallow lagoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们下方的一座环礁围着一片浅潟湖。
senses.why: the word names the whole ring, not one part of it, because the ring is what makes the feature recognisable from the air.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名整个环，而非其中一部分，因为从空中辨认靠的正是这个环。

senses.title: The reef rim
senses.definition: the outer edge of the reef where waves break
senses.definitionCN: 礁体迎浪的外缘，即白浪破碎处
senses.example: Surf broke along the atoll rim all night.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜都有浪沿着环礁礁缘破碎。
senses.why: the rim is the part that meets the open ocean, so the word is used for the outer edge as well as for the whole ring.
senses.whyCN: 礁缘是与外海相接的部分，因此这个词也指外缘，而不只指整个环。

senses.title: The enclosed lagoon
senses.titleCN: 环内潟湖：被围住的浅水
senses.definition: the shallow water enclosed by the ring
senses.definitionCN: 被环礁围住的浅水区
senses.example: The atoll holds a lagoon barely ten metres deep.
senses.exampleCN: 这座环礁围出一个不足十米深的潟湖。
senses.why: the ring exists by enclosing something, so the enclosed water is treated as part of the atoll's description.
senses.whyCN: 环的意义在于围住什么，因此被围的水也被视为环礁描述的一部分。

senses.title: Islets on the rim
senses.definition: low sandy islets built on parts of the reef
senses.definitionCN: 在礁体部分地段堆起的低矮沙岛
senses.example: Three islets rise only two metres above the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 环礁上的三座小岛只高出海面两米。
senses.why: sand and coral rubble collect on the rim, so the word also names the land that the reef carries.
senses.whyCN: 沙与珊瑚碎屑堆在礁缘，因此这个词也命名礁体承载的陆地。

senses.title: Formation by subsidence
senses.titleCN: 成因：火山基座沉降与珊瑚上长
senses.definition: the geological history in which a volcanic base subsides while coral grows upward
senses.definitionCN: 火山基座下沉、珊瑚向上生长所形成的地质历史
senses.example: Darwin explained the atoll by slow subsidence of a volcanic base.
senses.exampleCN: 达尔文用火山基座的缓慢沉降解释环礁的成因。
senses.why: the ring shape records a history: coral keeps building at the edge while the centre sinks.
senses.whyCN: 环形记录了一段历史：珊瑚在边缘持续建造，中央则在下沉。

senses.title: A human home
senses.titleCN: 人类居所：低岛上的生活
senses.definition: the land and water used as a home by island communities
senses.definitionCN: 被岛上社群当作居所的陆与水
senses.example: The atoll supports a fishing village of two hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这座环礁供养着一个两百人的渔村。
senses.why: a ring of islets with sheltered water is a practical place to live, so the word also names a human territory.
senses.whyCN: 一圈小岛加一片受护的水面是实用的居所，因此这个词也命名人类的地域。

senses.title: An ancient limestone body
senses.titleCN: 古环礁：抬升后的石灰岩体
senses.definition: a fossil atoll uplifted and exposed as limestone
senses.definitionCN: 被抬升出露、成为石灰岩的化石环礁
senses.example: The quarry cuts through an ancient atoll.
senses.exampleCN: 采石场切穿一座古环礁。
senses.why: when the seafloor rises, the reef becomes solid rock, and geology keeps the name for the fossil shape.
senses.whyCN: 海底抬升后礁体变成坚硬的岩石，地质学仍用这个词称呼那个化石形状。

senses.title: A low, exposed coast
senses.titleCN: 低洼而脆弱的环礁海岸
senses.definition: the atoll considered as a low-lying coast vulnerable to waves and rising sea
senses.definitionCN: 作为低洼、易受浪与海面上涨影响的环礁海岸
senses.example: Rising seas threaten every atoll in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 海面上涨威胁着这个地区的每一座环礁。
senses.why: the land sits only metres above the sea, so the word has become a shorthand for that vulnerability.
senses.whyCN: 陆地只高出海面数米，因此这个词已成为那种脆弱性的代称。

intro.en: Atoll entered English through French from Dhivehi, the language of the Maldives, where atolu names a reef ring. It has no Latin ancestry. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: atoll 经法语从马尔代夫的迪维希语进入英语，当地语 atolu 指环形礁。它没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Atolu in Dhivehi named the ring reefs of the Maldive islands, a navigational fact long known to local sailors.
items.cn: 迪维希语 atolu 指马尔代夫群岛的环形礁，这是当地水手早已知晓的航行事实。

items.en: French naturalists adopted the word in the early nineteenth century as atoll, spelling it after their own conventions.
items.cn: 十九世纪初法国博物学家借入这个词作 atoll，并按法语习惯拼写。

items.en: English took atoll from French in the 1830s, at first only for the Maldive and Caroline rings.
items.cn: 英语于十九世纪三十年代从法语借入 atoll，最初只用于马尔代夫与加罗林群岛的环礁。

items.en: Darwin's subsidence theory of 1842 gave the word a geological definition and spread it through science.
items.cn: 达尔文一八四二年的沉降说赋予这个词地质定义，并使它在科学界传播。

items.en: Twentieth-century oceanography mapped atolls worldwide and added the climate sense of a low, exposed coast.
items.cn: 二十世纪海洋学测绘了全球环礁，并加入「低洼脆弱海岸」的气候义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Dhivehi source of atolu is not established, and any Sanskrit or Indo-Aryan form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源存疑）：atolu 在迪维希语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的梵语或印度-雅利安语形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the reef types routinely confused with an atoll; group two holds the general landform words nearby in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是常与环礁混淆的礁类型；第二组是语义相近的一般地貌词。

entries.definition: A reef running parallel to a coast and separated from it by a lagoon; it does not close into a ring.
entries.definitionCN: 与海岸平行、被潟湖隔开的礁带；它并不闭合成环。

entries.definition: A reef growing directly along a coastline with no lagoon between it and the land.
entries.definitionCN: 紧贴海岸生长、与陆地之间没有潟湖的礁。

entries.definition: The shallow water enclosed by a reef or sandbar; an atoll contains a lagoon but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 被礁或沙洲围住的浅水；环礁包含潟湖，但它本身不是潟湖。

entries.definition: A small low sandy island on a reef; it is one piece of an atoll's rim, not the whole ring.
entries.definitionCN: 礁上的低矮小沙岛；它只是环礁礁缘的一小段，不是整个环。

entries.definition: Any ridge of rock or coral near the surface; it need not form a ring and need not enclose water.
entries.definitionCN: 任何接近水面的岩脊或珊瑚脊；不必成环，也不必围住水。

entries.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water; it says nothing about coral or about a ring shape.
entries.definitionCN: 四周被水围住的陆地；不涉及珊瑚，也不涉及环形。

entries.definition: A group or chain of islands; it is a regional grouping, not a single ring reef.
entries.definitionCN: 一组或一串岛屿；它是区域性的岛群，不是单个环形礁。

entries.definition: A shallow area of sand or rock rising near the surface; it has no enclosing ring.
entries.definitionCN: 接近水面隆起的浅沙或浅岩区；没有围合的环。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real geography, real reef types and real formation steps, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的地貌、真实的礁类型与真实的形成步骤，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Atoll is a borrowed Pacific word, not a Latin one: the thing and the name travel together.
normal.cn: atoll 是借来的太平洋词汇，不是拉丁词：事物与名字一起传来。

normal.en: The shape is a ring: reef outside, lagoon inside, islets on the rim.
normal.cn: 形状是一个环：外面是礁，里面是潟湖，环上散着小岛。

normal.en: Formation order: volcano, fringing reef, barrier reef, atoll, as the base sinks.
normal.cn: 形成次序：火山、裙礁、堡礁、环礁，随基座下沉而演进。

normal.en: An atoll is not a lagoon: the atoll is the ring, the lagoon is the water inside it.
normal.cn: 环礁不是潟湖：环礁是那个环，潟湖是环里的水。

normal.en: Low elevation is the point: most atoll islets stand only a few metres above the sea.
normal.cn: 低海拔是关键：多数环礁小岛只高出海面几米。

abstract.en: An atoll is a reef that learned to draw a circle around its own disappearance.
abstract.cn: 环礁是一座学会围着自己消失之处画圈的礁。

abstract.en: It is a ring of stone keeping a shallow promise of safety.
abstract.cn: 它是一圈石头，守着一份浅浅的安全承诺。

abstract.en: The volcano is gone, and only its coral handwriting remains.
abstract.cn: 火山已经不在了，只剩它珊瑚写下的笔迹。

examples.en: The atoll is less than three metres above sea level at its highest point.
examples.cn: 这座环礁最高处不足海拔三米。

examples.en: Coral grew upward as the volcanic base of the atoll subsided.
examples.cn: 随着环礁的火山基座下沉，珊瑚向上生长。

examples.en: Fresh water lies in a thin lens beneath the atoll.
examples.cn: 环礁之下有一层薄薄的淡水透镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: atoll＝环礁；记成「一圈礁围着中间浅水」，成因是火山下沉、珊瑚上长，外面浪白，里面水静。

root: 借自迪维希语 atolu（环形礁），经法语 atoll 进入英语；无拉丁语源，迪维希语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ring: the whole reef, its rim, its lagoon, its islets, its subsidence history, its human home, its fossil limestone body and its exposed coast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个环展开：整圈礁、礁缘、潟湖、小岛、沉降历史、人类居所、化石石灰岩体与脆弱海岸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin white ring of breaking waves around a pale blue centre, with deep blue outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈细白浪线围着一片浅蓝，圈外是深蓝。

branches.en: RING AND RIM: the whole circle, then the outer edge where waves break.
branches.cn: 环与缘：先是整个圈，再是迎浪的外缘。

branches.en: WATER AND LAND INSIDE: the enclosed lagoon, then the islets on the rim.
branches.cn: 圈内的水与陆：先是被围的潟湖，再是礁缘的小岛。

branches.en: HISTORY IN STONE: subsidence explains the ring, and uplift turns it into limestone.
branches.cn: 石中的历史：沉降解释环的形成，抬升又把它变成石灰岩。

branches.en: HUMAN HOME: the ring becomes a territory with a village and a fishery.
branches.cn: 人类居所：环变成有村庄与渔场的领地。

branches.en: LOW COAST: the same ring is now a measure of vulnerability.
branches.cn: 低海岸：同一个环如今成了脆弱性的尺度。

intro.en: Atoll is a single borrowed noun with no internal morphology; its related vocabulary comes from geography and other languages.
intro.cn: atoll 是单一借入名词，内部没有构词结构；它的相关词汇来自地理学与其他语言。

latinIntro.en: Atoll has no Latin entries. Latin insula 'island' and Greek korallion 'coral' describe the same setting from unrelated roots.
latinIntro.cn: atoll 没有拉丁条目。拉丁 insula「岛」与希腊 korallion「珊瑚」用无关词根描述同一环境。

items.structure: atoll (English noun from French, from Dhivehi atolu)
items.example: The atoll lies far from any continent.
items.exampleCN: 这座环礁远离任何大陆。

items.structure: reef (English noun, from Old Norse rif 'ridge')
items.example: The reef protects the shore from swell.
items.exampleCN: 礁保护海岸不受涌浪冲击。

items.structure: lagoon (English noun from Italian laguna, from Latin lacuna)
items.meaning: shallow water enclosed by reef or sand
items.example: The lagoon is calm at low tide.
A motu rises on the northern rim.
items.exampleCN: 北侧礁缘上有一座小岛。

items.example: Palms grow on the cay.

items.meaning: a reef attached to the shore
items.example: A fringing reef runs along the island.

items.meaning: a reef separated from shore by a lagoon
items.example: The barrier reef shelters the bay.
Coral built the ring over millennia.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚用千年时间造出这个环。

items.example: Subsidence shaped the atoll.

definition_zh: 承认；认可；致谢；回执
definition_en: a statement that something is true or that someone deserves credit, or a signal confirming that something has been received
core_image: 收到一封重要的信，回一张签收条：我看见了，也承认它到了
scene: 会议结束时，主持人把每个人的贡献逐一点名。 Naming each person's contribution out loud was a public acknowledgment, and the receipt on the screen did the same for a message.
sceneCN: 这里 acknowledgment 是「承认、公开认可」（第 3 个义项：认可某人的贡献）；句意：把每个人的贡献当众点名是一种公开认可，屏幕上那条回执对一条消息做的也是同一件事。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、点名名单、屏幕上的回执提示、记录本。

derivatives.zh: 未被承认的；未得回应的

senses.title: Admitting that something is true
senses.definition: a statement or act showing that one accepts a fact as true
senses.definitionCN: 表明自己接受某一事实为真的陈述或行为
senses.example: There was a general acknowledgment that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 大家普遍承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: Acknowledge began as oncnāwan, 'to recognize, know'. To admit a fact is to say that you now know it and will not pretend otherwise, so the noun is a public form of recognition.
senses.whyCN: acknowledge 最初是 oncnāwan“认出、知道”。承认一个事实，就是说自己已经知道，并且不再假装不知道，因此这个名词是“认出”的公开形式。

senses.title: Admitting one's own fault
senses.definition: an admission that one has done something wrong or made a mistake
senses.definitionCN: 承认自己做了错事或犯了错误
senses.example: His acknowledgment of the error came only after the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之后，他才承认了这个错误。
senses.why: Recognition turns inward: the known fact is one's own act. The -ledge ending, borrowed from knowledge, reinforces the sense of owning a piece of knowledge about oneself.
senses.whyCN: “认出”转向内部：被知道的事实是自己的行为。借自 knowledge 的 -ledge 词尾加强了“拥有一份关于自己的知识”的感觉。

senses.title: Recognizing someone's contribution
senses.definition: an expression of credit or respect for a person's help, status, or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的帮助、地位或成就表示认可与尊重
senses.example: The director received an award in acknowledgment of her years of service.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主管因多年服务而获奖，得到认可。
senses.why: What is recognized here is not a fact but a person's worth. Acknowledgment makes the recognition public, which is why it often appears with awards, prefaces, and speeches.
senses.whyCN: 这里被“认出”的不是事实，而是某人的价值。承认使这种认出变得公开，因此它常与奖项、前言、演讲一起出现。

senses.title: Confirming that something arrived
senses.definition: a formal signal that a letter, message, or delivery has been received
senses.definitionCN: 表示信件、消息或货物已经收到的正式信号
senses.example: Please return the signed form as acknowledgment of receipt.
senses.exampleCN: 请把签好的表格寄回，作为收到回执。
senses.why: Communication needs proof that the message crossed the gap. Acknowledgment becomes a token: the words 'I have it' are replaced by a document or a signal that can be checked later.
senses.whyCN: 通信需要证明消息越过了那道缝。acknowledgment 于是成为凭证：“我收到了”这句话被一份可事后核查的文件或信号取代。

senses.title: The thanks page of a book
senses.definition: a section, usually at the front or back of a book, thanking those who helped
senses.definitionCN: 书籍前后用于感谢帮助者的部分
senses.example: She names the archivists in the acknowledgments.
senses.exampleCN: 她在致谢部分列出了档案管理员的姓名。
senses.why: A book is a collaborative object that carries one author's name. The acknowledgments section is where the hidden recognition is printed, turning private gratitude into a permanent public record.
senses.whyCN: 书是协作的产物，却只署一个作者的名字。致谢部分就是隐藏的“认出”被印出来的地方，把私人的感激变成永久的公共记录。

senses.title: A signal that data arrived
senses.definition: in computing, a message sent back to confirm that data or a request was received
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中返回以确认数据或请求已收到的消息
senses.example: The server waits for an acknowledgment before sending the next packet.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器在发送下一个数据包前会等待一个确认。
senses.why: Networks inherit the postal receipt: a packet without an acknowledgment is only a guess. The word's old sense of 'confirming arrival' becomes a protocol event.
senses.whyCN: 网络继承了邮政回执：没有确认的数据包只是一次猜测。这个词古老的“确认抵达”义变成一个协议事件。

senses.title: Diplomatic recognition
senses.definition: a formal act by which one state recognizes another state or government
senses.definitionCN: 一国正式承认另一国或其政府的行为
senses.example: The treaty was followed by mutual acknowledgment of the new state.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订后，双方承认了这个新国家。
senses.why: At the level of states, recognition is a legal act with consequences: a government that is acknowledged can sign, sue, and be sued. The noun becomes an instrument of international law.
senses.whyCN: 在国家层面，承认是有法律后果的行为：被承认的政府可以签约、起诉与被起诉。这个名词于是成为国际法工具。

senses.title: A legal admission of a claim
senses.titleCN: 法律上对债务或主张的承认
senses.definition: a formal statement, especially in law, admitting that a debt, right, or claim exists
senses.definitionCN: 法律中正式承认债务、权利或主张存在
senses.example: The debtor signed an acknowledgment of the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 债务人签署了一份债务承认书。
senses.why: Law converts a spoken admission into evidence. An acknowledgment stops the person from later denying the claim, so the word becomes a written act rather than a state of mind.
senses.whyCN: 法律把口头承认变成证据。承认书使当事人日后不能否认该主张，因此这个词变成书面行为，而不是心理状态。

intro.en: Acknowledgment is a double derivative: the verb acknowledge plus -ment. Acknowledge itself is a Middle English reshaping of Old English oncnāwan 'to recognize', with -ledge inserted by analogy with knowledge.
intro.cn: acknowledgment 是双重派生：动词 acknowledge 加 -ment。acknowledge 本身是中古英语对古英语 oncnāwan“认出”的改写，其中 -ledge 是类比 knowledge 插进去的。

items.en: Oncnāwan means 'to know, recognize, understand', from on- plus cnāwan 'to know'. The core is recognition, not confession.
items.cn: oncnāwan 意为“知道、认出、理解”，由 on- 加 cnāwan“知道”构成。核心是“认出”，不是“忏悔”。

items.en: The verb becomes aknowen, then acknowledge. The -ledge element is inserted in the 16th century by association with knowledge; it is not an independent suffix with meaning.
items.cn: 这个动词先作 aknowen，后作 acknowledge。16 世纪时，因与 knowledge 联想而插入 -ledge 成分；它并不是一个有独立含义的后缀。

items.en: The noun suffix -ment comes from Latin -mentum through French and forms nouns of action or result. Acknowledgment can therefore name both the act of recognizing and the document that records it.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ment 经法语来自拉丁语 -mentum，构成动作或结果名词。因此 acknowledgment 既能指“认出”的行为，也能指记录它的文件。

items.en: The noun spreads from personal admission to formal receipt and to credit for help. Legal and commercial uses fix the documentary sense.
items.cn: 16 至 17 世纪，这个名词从个人承认扩展到正式回执与对帮助的致谢。法律与商业用法固定了它的文书义。

items.en: Computing adds the packet acknowledgment, and diplomacy keeps the state-recognition sense. The word now covers a feeling, a paragraph, a receipt, and a protocol signal.
items.cn: 20 世纪，计算机增加了数据包确认，外交保留国家承认义。这个词如今覆盖一种态度、一段文字、一张回执，以及一个协议信号。

note.en: The first group shares the acknowledg- shape or the same 'know' root; the second compares words for admitting and recognizing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 acknowledg- 外形或同一“知道”词根；第二组比较表示“承认与认可”的词。

normal.en: acknowledge began as 'recognize': on + cnāwan, to know. Admitting is saying 'I know this' out loud.
normal.cn: acknowledge 最初是“认出”：on + cnāwan，知道。承认就是大声说“我知道这件事”。

normal.en: The -ledge is borrowed from knowledge: it looks like a suffix but is a piece of analogy.
normal.cn: -ledge 是从 knowledge 借来的：它看起来像后缀，其实是一块类比。

abstract.en: An acknowledgment does not create the fact; it only removes the possibility of pretending.
abstract.cn: 承认并不创造事实，它只是移除了“假装不知道”的可能。

abstract.en: Every message needs a return signal, and every person needs one too.
abstract.cn: 每条消息都需要一个返回信号，每个人也需要一个。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（使）+ know（知道）+ -ledge（借自 knowledge）+ -ment → 使知道成为公开确认 → 承认、致谢、回执

dict_mnemonic.text: demographer ＝ demo（人民）＋ graph（写、记录）＋ er（人）＝把人民的情况记录下来的人，「人口学家」。

root: 希腊语 dēmos（人民）＋ graphia（记录）→ demography（人口学）＋ -er（人）→ demographer

sensesIntro.en: One person counting people: a chart, a register and a pension plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个数人的人：一张图、一本登记册与一份养老金计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a researcher with three columns of records open and a pen resting on an age pyramid
core.cn: 核心意象：一位研究者摊开三栏登记册，笔尖停在年龄金字塔图上

branches.en: A pen resting on an age pyramid chart.
branches.cn: 一支停在年龄金字塔图上的笔。

branches.en: Three columns of a register laid side by side.
branches.cn: 三栏并排摊开的登记册。

branches.en: A pension spreadsheet with a falling birth line.
branches.cn: 一张出生曲线往下走的养老金表格。

branches.en: Both turn records into a picture of a population.
branches.cn: 两者都把记录变成人口的图景。

branches.en: Both feed numbers into public decisions.
branches.cn: 两者都把数字送进公共决策。

intro.en: Demographer is demo- plus -graph- plus -er; the people-and-writing roots build the study family.
intro.cn: demographer 由 demo- 加 -graph- 加 -er 构成；人民与记录这两个词根造出学科一族词。

definition_zh: 刺耳的；音调不和谐的；嘈杂难听的
definition_en: having a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
core_image: 早高峰街口喇叭、钻孔与尖叫声搅成一团
scene: 清晨的工地边，钻机与汽车喇叭响成一片。 The street was cacophonous with drills and honking horns.
sceneCN: 这里 cacophonous 是「刺耳的、嘈杂的」（第 1 个义项：声音混杂难听）；句意是街上钻机与喇叭声搅作一团。

pos.zh: 刺耳的；不和谐的；嘈杂的

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「刺耳的声音；不和谐音」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「刺耳地；嘈杂地」
同根反义词，eu- 换 caco-，义为「悦耳的」

senses.title: Harsh in sound
senses.definition: unpleasant and harsh to the ear
senses.definitionCN: 听感不快、粗粝刺耳的
senses.example: The gulls made a cacophonous racket over the fish market.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥在鱼市上空发出刺耳的喧闹。
senses.why: The prefix caco- means bad and phone means sound.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 caco- 意为「坏」，phone 意为「声音」，合即「坏声音」。

senses.title: Discordant when mixed
senses.definition: made up of sounds that clash and do not blend
senses.definitionCN: 由相互冲突、无法融合的声音构成
senses.example: An orchestra tuning up is deliberately cacophonous.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队调音时的声音故意不和谐。
senses.why: Many bad sounds at once create discord rather than music.
senses.whyCN: 多种杂音并作便成失调，而非乐音。

senses.title: Jarring in language or style
senses.definition: of words or writing, harsh and awkward in sound
senses.definitionCN: 指词句发音粗硬拗口
senses.example: The poet chose cacophonous consonants to imitate the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人故意选用刺耳的辅音来模拟风暴。
senses.why: Sound aesthetics extends from music to speech.
senses.whyCN: 声音美学由音乐延伸至语言。

intro.en: Cacophonous is built on Greek roots: kakos, bad, and phone, sound.
intro.cn: cacophonous 由希腊语词根构成：kakos（坏）加 phone（声音）。

items.en: a root meaning bad or evil lies behind Greek kakos; the reconstruction is uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 希腊语 kakos 背后是表示「坏、恶」的原始印欧词根，细节属重构。

items.en: kakos meant bad, and phone meant sound or voice.
items.cn: 希腊语 kakos 意为「坏」，phone 意为「声音、嗓音」。

items.en: kakophonia named a harsh or ill-sounding phrase.
items.cn: 希腊语 kakophonia 指粗粝刺耳的言语。

items.en: French cacophonie brought the term into modern European usage.
items.cn: 法语 cacophonie 把这个词带入近代欧洲语用。

items.en: English formed the noun cacophony and the adjective cacophonous.
items.cn: 英语在十八至十九世纪由名词 cacophony 派生形容词 cacophonous。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound root; the near-meaning group gathers noise words.
note.cn: 形近组同出「声音」词根；近义组是噪声类词。

entries.definition: a harsh discordant mixture of sound
entries.definitionCN: 刺耳的混杂声，cacophonous 的名词

entries.definition: pleasing to the ear
entries.definitionCN: 悦耳的，同根反义

entries.definition: a sounding together, a musical form
entries.definitionCN: 交响乐，同出 phone 词根

entries.definition: a far-sounding device
entries.definitionCN: 电话，同出 phone 词根

entries.definition: not in agreement, as sounds
entries.definitionCN: 不和谐的；相冲突的

entries.definition: harsh and irritating in sound
entries.definitionCN: 粗粝刺耳的

entries.definition: loud and rough in voice
entries.definitionCN: 沙哑喧闹的

entries.definition: shockingly out of harmony
entries.definitionCN: 刺耳突兀的

entries.definition: loud, harsh and forceful
entries.definitionCN: 尖锐刺耳的

normalIntro.en: Break it once: caco, bad; phon, sound; ous, adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 拆一次就记住：caco 坏，phon 声，ous 形容词尾。

normal.en: Caco- means bad, as in cacophony.
normal.cn: caco- 意为「坏」，如 cacophony。

normal.en: -phon- means sound, as in telephone.
normal.cn: -phon- 意为「声音」，如 telephone。

normal.en: Euphonious is its opposite, good-sounding.
normal.cn: euphonious 是它的反义词，意为悦耳。

normal.en: A cacophony is the noun for the noise itself.
normal.cn: cacophony 是噪声的名词形式。

normal.en: Cacophony and cacophonous differ only in ending.
normal.cn: cacophony 与 cacophonous 仅词尾不同。

abstract.en: Hear all the car horns of a jam hit at once.
abstract.cn: 听堵车时所有喇叭同时按响。

abstract.en: Feel your teeth ache at the scrape of chalk.
abstract.cn: 感受粉笔刮擦声让牙根发酸。

abstract.en: Picture an orchestra tuning all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象乐队同时调音的一片杂响。

examples.en: The morning market opened in a cacophonous babble of vendors.
examples.cn: 清晨的集市在摊贩刺耳的喧声中开场。

examples.en: The score turns deliberately cacophonous to portray the battle.
examples.cn: 乐谱故意变得不和谐以描绘战斗。

examples.en: Cacophonous feedback howled from the broken speaker.
examples.cn: 坏掉的音箱发出刺耳的啸叫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡壳疯呢」——音响卡壳，疯了一样刺耳；一屋子人都被吵得抓狂。

root: cacophonous 出自希腊语 kakos「坏的」加 phone「声音」，经 kakophonia、法语 cacophonie 进入英语；同根词 euphonious（悦耳）、symphony（交响）、telephone（电话）都围着「声音」词根生长。

sensesIntro.en: Bad sound first, then the clash of many sounds, finally the harshness of words themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是「坏声音」，再是众多声音的冲突，最后落到语言本身的粗粝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rush-hour street where every horn shrieks at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：早高峰街口所有喇叭同时尖鸣。

branches.cn: 鱼市上空喧闹的海鸥

branches.cn: 引擎刺耳的轰鸣

branches.en: deliberate discord in music and verse
branches.cn: 音乐与诗中有意为之的失调

intro.cn: 这个词是透明的希腊语复合：坏加声音加形容词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 词根为希腊语，英语形容词形式经拉丁化的词尾构成。

definition_zh: 赎罪；弥补；补偿；（神学）和解
definition_en: the act of making amends for a wrong; reparation, especially in a religious sense
core_image: 天平一端放着过错，一端慢慢加上的弥补之石
scene: 教堂的烛光里，他把写满悔意的信一页页读完，然后起身走向那位多年未见的老友。 The letter was his atonement for the quarrel that split the family.
sceneCN: 这里 atonement 是「赎罪、弥补」（第 1 个义项：为过错所作的补偿行为）；句意为这封信是他为造成家庭分裂的争吵所作的补偿。

derivatives.zh: 动词本源，义为「赎罪；弥补」
由动词加人后缀构成，义为「赎罪者」

senses.title: The act of making amends
senses.definition: repayment or reparation for injury or wrong
senses.definitionCN: 对伤害或过错的偿还与补救
senses.example: Rebuilding the school was his atonement.
senses.exampleCN: 重建学校便是他的赎罪。
senses.why: From at one: amends reunite what the wrong divided.
senses.whyCN: 源自 at one：弥补使被过错拆散者重聚。

senses.title: Religious reconciliation with God
senses.definition: the reconciling of God and humanity, especially through sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 神人与解，尤指藉献祭达成的救赎
senses.example: The sermon spoke of atonement through sacrifice.
senses.exampleCN: 布道讲到藉献祭而得的救赎。
senses.why: Theology kept the oldest sense: sin tears, sacrifice restores oneness.
senses.whyCN: 神学保留了最古老的意义：罪使人撕裂，献祭恢复合一。

intro.en: Atonement is at one plus -ment, first written as two words meaning reconciliation, later fused into one theological term.
intro.cn: atonement 由 at one 加 -ment 构成，初作两词写作、意为和解，后凝缩为神学术语。

items.en: An meant one.
items.cn: 古英语 an 意为一。

items.en: At one described setting disputants at unity.
items.cn: 中古英语 at one 表示使争执者归于一体。

items.en: Tyndale coined atonement to render Greek reconciliation in the New Testament.
items.cn: 十六世纪廷代尔以 atonement 翻译《新约》中的「和好」一词。

items.en: It became the fixed theological noun for Christ's reconciling work.
items.cn: 它成为指基督救赎之工的固定神学名词。

items.en: Everyday use now covers any formal or moral amends.
items.cn: 如今日常用法泛指一切正式或道德上的补偿。

note.en: Atonement is the price and the process of becoming at one again.
note.cn: atonement 是重新「合而为一」的代价与过程。

examples.en: The novel is a study in guilt and atonement.

definition_zh: 工业社会（以工业生产为主导的社会形态）
definition_en: a society whose economy and daily life are organized around manufacturing industry
core_image: 厂房、工人宿舍、铁路与钟楼围成一座自足的城市，汽笛决定一天的节奏
scene: 老照片里，上班的人流在天未亮时涌向厂门，汽笛一响整条街都醒了。 Industrial society brought the factory clock into everyday life.
sceneCN: 这里 industrial society 指「以工业生产为主导组织起来的社会」（第 1 个义项：以制造业为基础的社会）；句意为工业社会把工厂的时钟带进了日常生活。图中可辨识物件：厂房、宿舍、铁路、钟楼、涌向厂门的人流。

senses.title: A society built on manufacturing
senses.titleCN: 以制造业为基础的社会
senses.definition: a society whose wealth, work and daily rhythm centre on factory production
senses.definitionCN: 财富、工作与日常节奏都以工厂生产为中心的社会
senses.example: Industrial society brought the factory clock into everyday life.
senses.exampleCN: 工业社会把工厂的时钟带进了日常生活。
senses.why: the phrase simply names a society of the industrial kind, with industry as its organizing centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语直接命名一种工业类型的社会，以工业为其组织中心。

senses.title: A stage in development typology
senses.titleCN: 发展阶段类型中的一个阶段
senses.definition: one stage in the classification that runs from agrarian to industrial to post-industrial societies
senses.definitionCN: 从农业社会到工业社会再到后工业社会的分类中的一个阶段
senses.example: Sociologists placed the country at the industrial stage of the typology.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学者把这个国家归入类型学中的工业阶段。
senses.why: a type becomes a stage when societies are arranged along a single line of development.
senses.whyCN: 当社会被排在同一条发展线上时，一个类型就变成一个阶段。

senses.title: A concept in early sociology
senses.titleCN: 早期社会学的一个概念
senses.definition: the model of modern society that nineteenth-century sociology built around industry and its division of labour
senses.definitionCN: 19 世纪社会学围绕工业及其分工所建立的现代社会模型
senses.example: Industrial society was the central concept of the discipline's founders.
senses.exampleCN: 工业社会是该学科创立者们的核心概念。
senses.why: early sociologists needed a name for the new order they saw replacing agrarian life.
senses.whyCN: 早期社会学者需要给眼前取代农业生活的新秩序一个名字。

senses.title: Its class and work structure
senses.definition: the social order of wage labour, employers and classes that factory production creates
senses.definitionCN: 工厂生产所造成的雇佣劳动、雇主与阶级的社会秩序
senses.example: Industrial society produced a large working class and a small owning class.
senses.exampleCN: 工业社会产生了一个庞大的工人阶级与一个很小的有产阶层。
senses.why: the factory gathers many workers under one employer, and that arrangement shapes the whole class structure.
senses.whyCN: 工厂把许多工人聚到同一个雇主之下，这一安排塑造了整个阶级结构。

senses.title: Its characteristic institutions
senses.definition: the school, the bureaucracy, the clock and the city that industrial organization requires
senses.definitionCN: 工业组织所需要的学校、官僚机构、时钟与城市
senses.example: Compulsory schooling was an institution of industrial society.
senses.exampleCN: 义务教育是工业社会的一项制度。
senses.why: industry needs punctual, literate, disciplined workers, so it builds institutions that produce them.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要守时、识字、守纪律的工人，因此它建起生产这类人的制度。

senses.title: A historical period
senses.definition: the era, roughly from the late eighteenth to the late twentieth century, when industry dominated
senses.definitionCN: 大约从 18 世纪末到 20 世纪末、工业占主导的时代
senses.example: The photographs document industrial society at its height.
senses.exampleCN: 这些照片记录了工业社会的鼎盛时期。
senses.why: a social type with a beginning and an end becomes a period that historians can date.
senses.whyCN: 一个有始有终的社会类型会成为历史学者可以断代的时期。

senses.title: The contrast with post-industrial society
senses.definition: the older order against which service-based and knowledge-based societies define themselves
senses.definitionCN: 以服务业与知识为基础的社会用来定义自身的那个较早秩序
senses.example: Post-industrial society is defined by what industrial society was not.
senses.exampleCN: 后工业社会是靠工业社会「不是」什么来定义的。
senses.why: once a successor type is named, the older phrase becomes a benchmark rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 一旦后继类型被命名，较早的短语就成为基准，而不只是描述。

senses.title: A target of ecological critique
senses.definition: the order criticized for treating nature as a supply of inputs and for generating risk
senses.definitionCN: 被批评为把自然当作投入来源并制造风险的那种秩序
senses.example: Green theorists blame industrial society for the climate crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色理论家把气候危机归咎于工业社会。
senses.why: critics turn the descriptive phrase into an accusation by attaching pollution and risk to its way of producing.
senses.whyCN: 批评者把污染与风险归到它的生产方式上，从而把描述性短语变成指控。

intro.en: Industrial is built on Latin industria 'diligence, activity'; society comes from Latin societas 'companionship, association', from socius 'ally'. The phrase belongs to nineteenth-century social thought. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: industrial 由拉丁 industria「勤勉、活动」构成；society 来自拉丁 societas「同伴关系、结社」，其词根为 socius「盟友」。这个短语属于 19 世纪的社会思想。年代均为约数。

items.en: Industria meant 'diligence, purposeful activity'; its deeper origin is unsettled, and the derivation sometimes offered from indu- plus struere 'to build' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: industria 意为「勤勉、有目的的活动」；其更深来源尚无定论，有人提出它由 indu- 与 struere「建造」构成，那只是假说。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally', and societas named the bond or association among such people. The deeper origin of socius is not established.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」，societas 指这些人之间的纽带或结社。socius 的更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Industry shifted from diligence to manufacturing in the eighteenth century, and industrial was coined to describe it.
items.cn: industry 在 18 世纪从「勤勉」转向「制造业」，industrial 随之被造出来描述它。

items.en: Society entered English through French and came to mean an organized collectivity, not merely company.
items.cn: society 经法语进入英语，逐渐指有组织的集体，而不只是作伴。

items.en: Social thinkers of the nineteenth century paired the two words to name the new order built on factories, wage labour and cities.
items.cn: 19 世纪的社会思想家把这两个词配对，用来命名建立在工厂、雇佣劳动与城市之上的新秩序。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origins and first date): the pre-Latin origins of industria and socius are reconstructions, and the earliest use of the exact phrase is not precisely recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：industria 与 socius 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式；这一确切短语的最早使用没有精确记录。

note.en: Group one holds industrial compounds and related words that look alike; group two holds other labels for modern social orders.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的工业类组合词与相关词；第二组是对现代社会秩序的其他称谓。

entries.definition: The economic order of privately owned industry and wage labour; it names the system, while industrial society names the society.
entries.definitionCN: 私有工业与雇佣劳动的经济秩序；命名的是制度，而工业社会命名的是社会。

entries.definition: A society that has completed industrialization, stressing the outcome rather than the social type.
entries.definitionCN: 已完成工业化的社会，强调结果而非社会类型。

entries.definition: The system of industrial organization, or belief in it as the proper basis of society.
entries.definitionCN: 工业组织的制度，或对其作为社会适当基础的信念。

entries.definition: The period of rapid mechanization that produced industrial society; the phrase names the change, not the resulting order.
entries.definitionCN: 带来工业社会的快速机械化时期；命名的是变化，而非形成后的秩序。

entries.definition: A society whose economy centres on services and knowledge rather than manufacturing.
entries.definitionCN: 经济以服务业与知识而非制造业为中心的社会。

entries.definition: A society organized around farming and land ownership, the type industrial society replaced.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕农业与土地所有权组织的社会，是工业社会所取代的类型。

entries.definition: A broad label for contemporary social orders; it includes industry but also politics, science and culture.
entries.definitionCN: 对当代社会秩序的宽泛称谓；包含工业，也包含政治、科学与文化。

entries.definition: A society of large-scale, impersonal organization and mass culture; it overlaps with industrial society but stresses conformity.
entries.definitionCN: 以大规模、非人格化组织与大众文化为特征的社会；与工业社会重叠，但强调趋同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Industrial describes the economy, society the people, so the phrase is a society organized around industry.
normal.cn: 工业的描述经济，社会的指人群，因此这个短语是围绕工业组织起来的社会。

normal.en: The typology runs agrarian, industrial, post-industrial in that order.
normal.cn: 类型学按农业、工业、后工业的顺序排列。

normal.en: The factory clock, the school and the city are its institutions.
normal.cn: 工厂时钟、学校与城市是它的制度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as mature industrial society and transition to an industrial society mark the historical senses.
normal.cn: 成熟的工业社会、向工业社会过渡这类固定搭配标出历史义。

normal.en: The phrase is descriptive, but critics turn it into an accusation.
normal.cn: 这个短语本为描述，但批评者会把它变成指控。

abstract.en: Picture a town whose bell tower has been replaced by a whistle nobody can ignore.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇的钟楼被一只谁也躲不开的汽笛取代。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom, a factory and a railway station built from the same grey brick.
abstract.cn: 想象教室、工厂与车站都用同一种灰砖建成。

abstract.en: Picture a river that carries goods instead of fish.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河里运的是货物而不是鱼。

examples.en: Industrial society expanded schooling to produce literate workers.
examples.cn: 工业社会扩张学校教育，以培养识字工人。

examples.en: The novel describes industrial society through one factory town.
examples.cn: 这部小说通过一座工厂城镇描写工业社会。

examples.en: Critics of industrial society pointed to pollution and alienation.
examples.cn: 工业社会的批评者指出了污染与疏离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「工业的（industrial）+ 社会（society）」——工厂与汽笛组织起来的社会，就是工业社会

root: 拉丁 industria「勤勉、活动」→ industrial；拉丁 socius「同伴」→ societas「结社」→ society。两词在 19 世纪社会思想中固定连用。两词的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one kind of society: the factory-centred order, its place in a typology, its role in early sociology, its class structure, its institutions, its historical period, its contrast with the post-industrial, and its use as an ecological accusation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种社会展开：以工厂为中心的秩序、它在类型学中的位置、它在早期社会学中的角色、它的阶级结构、它的制度、它的历史时期、它与后工业的对照，以及它作为生态指控的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a factory gate, a whistle, a school and a station all set within one grey town.
core.cn: 核心意象：厂门、汽笛、学校与车站都装在同一座灰色城镇里。

branches.en: CENTRE: the base sense, a society whose working life turns around manufacturing.
branches.cn: 中心：基础义，工作生活围绕制造业运转的社会。

branches.en: PLACE IN TIME: a stage in the typology and, later, a dated historical period.
branches.cn: 时间中的位置：类型学中的一个阶段，后来又成为一个可断代的时期。

branches.en: MODEL AND CLASSES: a concept built by early sociology, and the wage-labour order it described.
branches.cn: 模型与阶级：早期社会学建立的概念，以及它所描述的雇佣劳动秩序。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: the clock, the school and the city that industry requires.
branches.cn: 制度：工业所需的时钟、学校与城市。

branches.en: AFTERWARD AND AGAINST: the benchmark set by post-industrial society, and the ecological charge laid against it.
branches.cn: 之后与反对：后工业社会树立的基准，以及针对它的生态指控。

intro.en: The phrase joins an adjective of industry to a noun of association, and both halves carry productive pieces.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个工业形容词与一个结社名词连在一起，两半都带着能产的构词成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria gives industry, industrial and industrialization; Latin socius gives society, social and associate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 industria 给出 industry、industrial 与 industrialization；拉丁 socius 给出 society、social 与 associate。

items.example: The root first named effort, then manufacturing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先指努力，后来指制造业。

items.example: It forms the adjective of industry.
Industrial output doubled in a decade.
items.exampleCN: 工业产出在十年内翻番。

items.example: The root names people bound to one another.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指彼此联结的人。

items.example: It builds the noun of association.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结社的名词。

items.example: Society changes faster than its laws.
items.exampleCN: 社会的变化快于它的法律。

items.example: It builds the adjective from the noun of association.
items.exampleCN: 它由结社名词构成形容词。

items.example: Social rules vary between towns.
It names the industrial order as a system.
items.exampleCN: 它把工业秩序命名为一种制度。

items.meaning: the industrial system or its doctrine
items.example: Industrialism reshaped the family.

definition_zh: 经济增长；经济体产出总量的持续增加
definition_en: a sustained increase in the output of goods and services produced by an economy
core_image: 砖窑冒起新烟，外出的人回到镇上进厂，集市摊位一年比一年多
scene: 小镇的砖窑冒起新烟，年轻人从外地回来进厂，集市上的摊位一年比一年多，仓库也不得不加盖一排。 Economists point to rising output and call it economic growth.
sceneCN: 这里 economic growth 指「经济体产出总量的持续增加」（第 1 个义项：一国或一地区所生产的商品与服务总量不断上升）；句意为经济学家把产出上升称为经济增长。图中可辨识物件：冒烟的砖窑、回厂的年轻人、集市摊位、加盖的仓库。

senses.title: A sustained rise in output
senses.definition: a continuing increase in the goods and services an economy produces over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体随时间持续生产出更多商品与服务
senses.example: Economists point to rising output and call it economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家把产出上升称为经济增长。
senses.why: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective for the management of a household to a native noun for increase, so it names an increase of the whole organized economy.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把源自希腊语、指「家务管理」的形容词，与一个本族表示「增加」的名词组合起来，因此指整个有组织经济的增加。

senses.title: The growth rate
senses.definition: a percentage showing how fast output rises from one period to the next
senses.definitionCN: 表示产出从一个时期到下一个时期上升多快的百分数
senses.example: The economic growth rate averaged four percent that decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那十年间，经济增长率平均为百分之四。
senses.why: A process noun readily stands for its own measure, which is why the phrase can be followed by rate.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词容易转指自身的度量，因此这个短语后面可以直接接 rate。

senses.title: Growth per head
senses.definition: growth measured after dividing total output by the number of people, so that population change is taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 把总产出按人口分摊后再衡量的增长，从而把人口变动计入
senses.example: Per-head economic growth lagged behind the national total.
senses.exampleCN: 人均经济增长落后于全国总量。
senses.why: Because a larger population can raise the total while leaving each person no better off, the phrase is often qualified by per head.
senses.whyCN: 因为人口增加可以抬高总量而个人并未变好，这个短语常被加上「人均」的限定。

senses.title: Extensive growth
senses.definition: growth achieved by adding more land, labour and capital rather than by using them better
senses.definitionCN: 靠增加土地、劳动与资本投入而非提高使用效率来实现的增长
senses.example: Extensive economic growth ran out of new land to plough.
senses.exampleCN: 粗放型经济增长把可开垦的新地都用尽了。
senses.why: When the increase comes from more inputs, economists call it extensive, and the phrase takes the adjective as a label.
senses.whyCN: 当增加来自更多投入时，经济学家称之为粗放型，这个短语便带上该形容词作为标签。

senses.title: Intensive growth
senses.definition: growth achieved by raising productivity, so that the same inputs yield more output
senses.definitionCN: 靠提高生产率、使同样投入产出更多而实现的增长
senses.example: Intensive economic growth followed the rebuilding of the mills.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊重建之后，出现了集约型经济增长。
senses.why: The mirror label marks growth from better methods rather than from more hands, and the phrase carries both.
senses.whyCN: 这个镜像标签标记来自更好方法而非更多人工的增长，这个短语两者都能承载。

senses.title: The boom that growth brings
senses.definition: the period of fuller shops, more jobs and rising confidence that accompanies rising output
senses.definitionCN: 伴随产出上升而来的店铺更热闹、岗位更多、信心更高的时期
senses.example: Three years of economic growth filled the high street again.
senses.exampleCN: 三年的经济增长让商业街重新热闹起来。
senses.why: By metonymy the cause stands for its effects, so the phrase can name the prosperous stretch rather than the statistic.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，原因代替了结果，因此这个短语可以指那段繁荣时期，而不只是那个统计量。

senses.title: Sustainable growth
senses.definition: growth that does not exhaust the resources or damage the systems on which future output depends
senses.definitionCN: 不会耗尽资源、也不破坏未来产出所依赖的系统的增长
senses.example: Sustainable economic growth requires cleaner power.
senses.exampleCN: 可持续的经济增长需要更清洁的电力。
senses.why: Once the environmental cost is counted, the phrase takes a qualifier that asks whether the increase can continue.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把环境成本计入，这个短语就带上一个限定语，追问这种增加能否持续。

senses.title: Growth as a policy target
senses.definition: the pursuit of rising output as the chief aim of government policy
senses.definitionCN: 把产出上升当作政府政策的首要目标来追求
senses.example: The budget put economic growth ahead of every other aim.
senses.exampleCN: 预算把经济增长排在所有其他目标之前。
senses.why: A measured increase can become an objective, and the phrase then names a goal rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 一个被度量的增加可以变成目标，这个短语于是指一项追求而非一个事实。

intro.en: Economic growth joins economic, from Greek oikonomia 'household management' through Latin oeconomia and French économique, with growth, a native English noun from the verb grow. The phrase belongs to modern economics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: economic growth 由 economic 与 growth 组合而成；economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」，经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语 économique 进入英语；growth 则是英语本族名词，源自动词 grow。这个短语属于现代经济学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, household', the unit whose resources were to be managed.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、家户」，即其资源需要被管理的单位。

items.en: Oikos plus nomos 'managing, rule, custom' gave oikonomia, the art of running a household; nomos itself comes from nemein 'to manage, distribute'.
items.cn: oikos 加 nomos「管理、规则、习俗」构成 oikonomia，即治家之术；nomos 本身来自 nemein「管理、分配」。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as oeconomia, still meaning household management rather than a national economy.
items.cn: 拉丁把希腊词借作 oeconomia，仍指家务管理，而不是国家经济。

items.en: French économique supplied English economic in the seventeenth century; the sense 'of a national economy' developed later, in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 économique 在 17 世纪提供英语 economic；「属于国家经济」的义项则较晚，在 19 世纪发展出来。

items.en: Grow is native: Old English growan 'to grow, increase' is a strong verb whose past tense was grew and whose participle was grown.
items.cn: grow 是英语本族词：古英语 growan「生长、增加」是强变化动词，过去式为 grew，过去分词为 grown。

items.en: The phrase took its present meaning with national accounting and development economics in the twentieth century, when output could be measured year by year.
items.cn: 这个短语在 20 世纪随国民核算与发展经济学取得今义，当时产出已能逐年计量。

note.en: The first group holds phrases that are often substituted for this one but measure or mean something else; the second holds plain words for things getting larger.
note.cn: 第一组是常被拿来替换本短语、但所测或所指并不相同的说法；第二组是「变大」的朴素说法。

entries.definition: A wider idea that includes institutions, health, education and distribution, not only rising output.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的概念，包含制度、健康、教育与分配，而不只是产出上升。

entries.definition: The upswing of the business cycle; it may be shorter and more temporary than growth.
entries.definitionCN: 商业周期的上行段；可能比 growth 更短、更暂时。

entries.definition: The amount produced at a moment; growth is the change in that amount over time.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时点生产出的数量；growth 是这一数量随时间的变化。

entries.definition: The percentage by which output rises; it reports growth rather than naming the process.
entries.definitionCN: 产出上升的百分数；它报告增长，而不命名这个过程。

entries.definition: A literal description of the same fact, with no economic framing.
entries.definitionCN: 对同一事实的字面描述，不带经济学框架。

entries.definition: A rapid, often speculative upturn; it suggests intensity and eventual bust rather than steady gain.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速且常带投机的上行；暗示猛烈以及随后的回落，而非稳步增益。

entries.definition: A condition of comfort and success; it is a state people enjoy, not a measured increase.
entries.definitionCN: 富足顺遂的状态；是人们享受的境况，而非被度量的增加。

entries.definition: Growth as measured by gross domestic product; it is one yardstick of economic growth, not the whole idea.
entries.definitionCN: 以国内生产总值衡量的增长；是经济增长的一种尺子，而非全部。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Greek root, a native English verb and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、英语本族动词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oikos 'house' plus nomos 'management': the household whose output is now counted by the nation.
normal.cn: oikos「家」加 nomos「管理」：这个家户的产出如今由国家来计数。

normal.en: grow is native Old English; growth adds the noun suffix -th to the verb.
normal.cn: grow 是古英语本族词；growth 是在动词后加名词后缀 -th。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sustained economic growth, rapid economic growth, economic growth rate.
normal.cn: 固定说法：持续经济增长、快速增长、经济增长率。

normal.en: The pair is common in policy: promote growth, slow growth, inclusive growth.
normal.cn: 这对搭配常见于政策话语：促进增长、增长放缓、包容性增长。

normal.en: Keep growth apart from development: one is output, the other includes institutions and well-being.
normal.cn: 把 growth 与 development 分开：前者是产出，后者还包含制度与福祉。

abstract.en: Picture a brick kiln smoking again after years of silence.
abstract.cn: 想象一座沉寂多年的砖窑重新冒烟。

abstract.en: Picture a market that needs one more row of stalls each season.
abstract.cn: 想象集市每季都得多添一排摊位。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart climbing while a whole town changes underneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线往上走，整座小镇在它下面改变。

examples.en: Sustained economic growth lifted millions out of rural poverty.
examples.cn: 持续的经济增长使数百万人摆脱农村贫困。

examples.en: The report asks whether economic growth can continue without new energy sources.
examples.cn: 报告追问：没有新能源，经济增长能否持续。

examples.en: Per-head economic growth stalled even as the total rose.
examples.cn: 总量上升之际，人均经济增长却停滞了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「economic（经济的）+ growth（增长）」——经济这块蛋糕一年比一年大 → 经济增长

root: economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」= oikos「家」+ nomos「管理」→ 拉丁 oeconomia → 法语 économique → 英语 economic；growth 为古英语 growan「生长」加名词后缀 -th。短语义属 20 世纪国民核算。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one increase: total output rises, and then that rise is read as a rate, as a share per head, as more inputs, as better methods, as a boom, as a limit and finally as a policy aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个增加展开：总产出上升，这个上升再依次被读作一个比率、一份人均份额、更多投入、更好方法、一段繁荣、一条限度，最后是一项政策目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kiln smoking again, workers returning, and one more row of market stalls each season.
core.cn: 核心意象：砖窑重新冒烟，工人回厂，集市每季多出一排摊位。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND RATE: the increase itself, and the percentage that reports it.
branches.cn: 产出与比率：增加本身，以及报告它的百分数。

branches.en: SHARE AND BOOM: growth divided among people, and the fuller shops it brings.
branches.cn: 份额与繁荣：增长分到每个人头上，以及它带来的更热闹的店铺。

branches.en: INPUTS AND METHODS: the same increase can come from more hands or from better hands.
branches.cn: 投入与方法：同一种增加可以来自更多人手，也可以来自更巧的手。

branches.en: LIMIT: the question whether the increase can keep going without exhausting its base.
branches.cn: 限度：这种增加能否在不耗尽根基的情况下继续。

branches.en: AIM: a measured increase becomes something a government tries to produce.
branches.cn: 目标：一个被度量的增加，变成政府努力去促成的对象。

intro.en: The phrase can be read in five pieces: two Greek roots, a Latin borrowing, an adjective suffix, and a native English verb with its noun suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语可拆成五段：两个希腊词根、一个拉丁借词、一个形容词后缀，以及一个英语本族动词连同它的名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek oikos and nomos reached English through Latin oeconomia and French économique; grow is native Old English and has no Latin ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 oikos 与 nomos 经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语 économique 进入英语；grow 是古英语本族词，没有拉丁来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 economy 背后的「家户」意象。

items.example: The root names the ordering of the household.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指家户的秩序安排。

items.example: The compound is the direct ancestor of economy.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是 economy 的直系祖先。

items.example: Latin kept the household sense for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把「家户」义保留了许多世纪。

items.example: The modern sense is tied to national economies.
items.exampleCN: 现代义与国民经济相连。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由名词构成形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns grow into the noun growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 grow 变成名词 growth。
